q: Karl said that if he had a problem 'downstairs', he wouldn't go to the doctor. What would he do instead?
a: Show it to Suzanne and ask "Is that normal?"
x: Look it up in his mam's medical book
Wait and see if it cleared up by Christmas
Ask his dad to have a quick look

ex: I had to go to the doctor...
I'd show it to Suzanne and say "is that normal?" -

q: In Karl's Samson story, why didn't God just ask Noah for another favour?
a: It's like jury service: once you've done it, you're left alone for a bit
x: Noah was too seasick to work again
Noah's boat was still drying out
Noah wanted paying this time

ex: And then he had a word with Noah, he did the boat thing, so he said, I can't ask for two favors, right?
So he asked this other bloke, Manoah
He was happy with Noah though, was he?
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. He let him go on though, it's like jury service, once you've done it, you're left alone for a bit aren't you. So anyway

q: Karl's new freaks book had a fella with "one face, but two bodies". Why did Karl say it was mainly the face that was weird?
a: He looked fed up
x: He had a monobrow
He was winking
It was on upside down
f: Steve tried "Surely 'one head, two bodies'?" and later: "Roll up, roll up, see the man with one face!"
ex: Um, head as well, but it was mainly the face that was weird because he looked fed up.
What are you talking about, how can you have a face without a head?!
What are you talking about? How can you have- what do you mean? How did it join to the neck?
It did have a head, but the fact is it was weird that it had one face to me.
What do you mean?! If you've got one head, you'd have one face.
Yeah, I know, but it was just... it was the fact that he had one face and two bodies that I didn't think-
But why do you keep saying "one face and two bodies" as opposed to "one head and two bodies"?! We're all the man with one face!

q: Karl liked "one big slipper" from an innovations catalogue. Why did he say it beats a normal pair?
a: You can't nip to the shops in it, so it stays by the sofa
x: It's half the price of buying two
Your feet keep each other warm
Suzanne can put her feet in it too
f: Karl's cosy plan: "And you go, right, I'm in for the night now, where's me slipper?"
ex: Why do you think that's a good invention? One big slipper?
How is that better than two smaller slippers?

Because the problem is with slippers, right? You've already said how. You nip across the road in them, right? So you muck them up and you have to buy Some more. There's no way you'll be nipping to the shops in that one big one that will…

q: Karl's mam and dad moved to a tiny house. Why did his dad take an electric saw to the spare double bed?
a: To fit wardrobes in on either side of it
x: To get it up the narrow stairs
To make room for a fish tank
Because Karl's feet stuck out the end
f: The room was so small his dad thought "I can sort that out" and sawed off about eight inches, mattress and all.
ex: And, uh, they had this double bed and that was for, like, you know, when friends come 'round and that, they can stay there. But the problem was, he wanted to, sort of, put these wardrobes in the bedroom, right?
That went on either side of the bed--
Sort of wrapped around the bed.
Because- yeah. But, because the room was so small, he thought, "I can sort that out."
Right. And he sawed the bed--

Square eggs
Golden eggs

q: Karl claimed a lot of snakes are born with two heads. What did he say the two heads do, even though they share one body?
a: Fight each other for food
x: Take it in turns to sleep
Argue over which way to slither
Hiss in harmony

ex: Snakes, right, you’re talkin’ about snakes,
A lot of snakes are born with 2 heads. It’s like a f- it’s like a familiar type thing that happens to snakes.
Yeah. They take it for granted, don’t they!
All right? Snakes born, 2 heads, they’ll fight each other for food, even though it’s still the same body.

q: Shown a newspaper photo of naked rambler Steve Gough, why did Karl say the man wasn't really nude?
a: He had shoes, socks, a rucksack and a hat on
x: He'd painted a suit on himself
He was hiding behind an Ordnance Survey map
He had a towel tied round his waist
f: Karl's verdict, as relayed by Ricky: "He's not nude, he's just got his knob out."
ex: Don't know, he's just a nudist I suppose. There's a picture in there. Karl looked at it and went "Urgh, what's the point in that?". He went, "Well look at him, he's got shoes and socks on.".
..."he's got a rucksack on, he's got a hat on. He's not nude, he's just got his knob out".

q: Watching swimming on TV, what was Karl's complaint about the butterfly stroke?
a: It's hard work but doesn't make you go any faster
x: It splashes everyone in the next lane
It's named after the wrong insect
The swimmers look like they're drowning
f: Karl couldn't name the front crawl and called it "that stroke". Ricky: "don't do that 'that stroke' on radio it doesn't work".
ex: I don't- I don't know why they do that.
It's just hard work, it doesn't make you go any faster than the- say the, that stroke.
Yeah, don't do that "that stroke" on radio it doesn't work - the crawl, yeah.

q: Karl claimed people on their phones in the cinema wouldn't n***** him. What did he compare it to?

Watching telly in a pub
Eating chips at a football match
f: Karl: "when you go on the tube, and read a paper, there's loads of noise, but you can still concentrate." Ricky: "He's got you!"
ex: Loads of people could be on the phone in there, and it wouldn't sort of n***** ya.
Fine, well at least we've cleared that up.
Well, because it's like when you go on the tube, and read a paper, there's loads of noise, but you can still concentrate.
Do you know what I mean.

You'd be too tired to go to work the next day

ex: Ronan. I just was, uh, telling you the other day about, you know, that song that he does. Uh (singing)'”Loving every day as if it's your last....one”
I was just thinking was, he’s saying that as if, like; oh, have a good day? But I reckon if he knew it was your last day I don't think you'd been in the mood to do anything

It doesn't do anything all day

Is that good? Is that exciting?
No, I think they've had an okapi born.
It's got a long nose, it's like a sort of tapir type thing.
Not interested. Have I said to you before about if an animal is named after what it eats, how interesting is it?

q: In Karl's diary, Oxfam was selling animals for Africa. Why did Karl wonder about buying one to keep in this country instead?
a: As a pet for his mam, who'd missed having one since the cat
x: To carry his shopping home
As a birthday present for Suzanne
To keep his lawn trimmed
f: Alpacas were 20 quid and donkeys 50. Karl: "50 quid's 50 quid and they're not bothered if they're selling alpaca to Africa."
ex: Got some posts from Oxfam. They're flogging animals for Africa again. They've got new animals in their catalogue now. They've got donkeys and alpacas, donkey's 50 quid, alpaca's 20 pains. I don't know if this is a special rate or if I…
Sorry, you don't get it. If you buy that for someone, you don't get it.
Yeah, but they're not bothered where they're going.
Yes, they do. Of course they don't. They don't deliver them. It's not like they're in a warehouse. Wonder people thinking, I hope people buy this. They're gonna put them out there.
But at the end of the day, 50 quid's 50 quid and they're not bothered if they're selling alpaca to Africa.
And I'm saying, can you get one to London? To them that is less hassle, right?

q: Ricky said the hose pipe in Egyptian toilets must be cleaner than paper. What did Karl compare it to?
a: Washing a car with a hose but no sponge
x: Watering the garden in the rain
A dentist's spit sink
Rinsing chips under the tap
f: Karl: "It's like when you clean a car: Yeah, use a hose, but where's the sponge?" Steve: "You rinse off a plate but then you always do a little wipe as well."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The Earth · 2010
ex: Well, they have a hose pipe, yeah. But I didn't fancy that.
Well, that's cleaner, though, isn't it? A hose pipe, really gonna get a proper wash
No! 'Is it heck'! 'Is it heck'! How can it be?!
Because that's not... going to clean it properly. It's going to get rid of some bits, innit? It's like when you clean a car: Yeah, use a hose, but where's the sponge?
Sure. You rinse off a plate but then you always do a little wipe as well.

q: Karl tests sayings to see if they work. In ASDA with Suzanne, which cake made him rethink "you can't have your cake and eat it"?
a: A comedy one shaped like a big pair of breasts
x: One shaped like a giant spoon
One that was already half eaten
A see-through one in a glass box

ex: A lot more, see if they work. Well, one-one that, um, happened a couple weeks ago, right? You were talking about it. The, uh- "you can’t, you can’t have your cake and eat it."

Well, I never understood that cause I thought well, what's the point of having your cake and not eating it, rather like your lap dancing analogy. But it actually means you can’t have eaten your cake and still have it there, obviously.
Well, the-the time that I saw that same work, right? I was in, I was in ASDA with Suzanne.
And d’you know those big…binders you get with nice cakes in ‘em?

a: "And an alarm went off and it was all a dream."
x: "And then we all had chips for tea."
"And then I had to go to bed."
"And they all lived happily ever after."

ex: The stories I did earlier on were, you know, you made ‘em up, but it was that thing that I’d always end ‘em with--
“And an alarm went off and it was all a dream.”
Yeah, yeah. But they didn’t, they didn’t- I mean, it was a bit of a--
“I bought some potatoes and some bread, but I woke up and it was all a dream.”

They gobble the beans too quickly
The farmers tickle their tummies

ex: Yeah, and then you also told me that there's a place where they grow coffee where the weasels come out
And eat the coffee, right, but they have too much of it and vomit. And they sell the vomit because it makes the coffee smoother.
When you say it like that it sounds ridiculous.

A politician dodging questions

ex: That's it - I'm taking her out.
What, you haven't got- you haven't got a present?
No, because we speant a lot this year--

Don't forget that's half yours, though. You're gonna be eating- you're not going to be- you're not just going to be sittin' there watching her eat going, "Oh, I'm hungry but I speant all-", you're gonna be eatin' as well. That's half yours.

q: On Christmas Day, Karl's mam opened the Victoria Plum and said 'Oh, that's nice'. How did she explain slagging it off when he'd shown it to her in the shop?
a: She thought he'd been pointing at something else
x: She was pretending, to keep it a surprise
She'd been in a bad mood that day
She hadn't had her glasses on
f: Karl had warned her "Don't bother openin' it" but handed it over anyway: "it's too late, I'd already bought it!"
ex: "Don't bother openin' it", she said, "No, no, why?"
OH NOO! Why did you still give it to her?!
So- well it's too late, I'd already bought it!

So she opened it and I was like, (Exhales) and she said, "Oh, that's nice", I said, "Why you sayin' that?", I said, "The other day you said it's bloody awful". She said, "No, no, I thought you were pointing at something else."
So that's why I don't get anyone anything anymore.

Suzanne wouldn't let him

So this is the same as you had one fight with Leroy, you went along to a dance studio with shut, you've seen Hilda's arse, and it's turned you off... proctology.
Once again, you just abandoned it!
Have a go. Just feel inside Hilda's back passage. Feel the blockage!
No, because the audience have already decided. They've seen a weakness in me, they're going to vote me out. There's no point me getting dirty fingers for this!

Whether Steve had to leave the room
Whether he could use a stick

And what are the rules though? Can I wear gloves?
No, no, just-just, you know...let's start off simple: would you take off my shoes and socks?

Her new false teeth

Auntie Nora. Umm, she was on a lot of medication and stuff.
And I think that’s a side effect, that comes with it. So, um, yeah, she had wind for five minutes, so I thought we’d dig that one out. Classic line, uh... Me Auntie Had Wind For Five Minutes.

It'd ask the ticket inspector
It'd hop on whatever's going north

Someone called up and said I don’t think a flea’s very good, how would the flea know…tell him, tell him what you said. He said how would the flea know what train to get on? He went he’d get to Euston and look at the timetable.
Yeah, and he went, he went, we’re not going to agree on this. He got annoyed at him because the bloke said it’d, he’d better to be a wasp.

A wasp would not survive would it, on, y’know, a Virgin train or something.
It just wouldn’t because people really don’t like wasps so somebody would end up clouting it and killing it and that brain would never get to his body, so…

A puffin
